Use 0W-20 synthetic oil and check levels every 1,000 miles. Some owners switch to 5W-30 for reduced consumption.

rows.title: Brake Actuator Buzzing and Grinding Noise

rows.title: 1MZ-FE V6 Engine Oil Sludge Failure
rows.howToFix: If oil gelling or sludge is suspected, stop driving when an oil-pressure warning, abnormal engine noise or loss of oil pressure is present and have the engine inspected under current VIN-specific Lexus service information. The Lexus special policy was historical, so this page does not promise a free repair in 2026. Do not use chemical flushes, repeated 1,000-2,000-mile flushing intervals, a viscosity change or a universal teardown instruction from this page. Follow the owner-manual oil specification and maintenance schedule unless current Lexus service information directs otherwise. No universal retail part or dealer-only remedy is asserted.

rows.title: Water Pump Premature Failure
rows.howToFix: Replace the water pump assembly and thermostat together as a preventive measure. Use OEM or high-quality aftermarket parts (Aisin brand is the OEM supplier). Replace the serpentine belt and tensioner at the same time if they show wear.

rows.title: 2JZ-GE Timing Belt Service - Interval Confusion and Interference Engine Risk
rows.howToFix: Replace the timing belt at 90,000 miles per Lexus factory schedule (do not stretch to Supra's 110k interval on a Lexus chassis). Replace the hydraulic tensioner, idler pulley, water pump, thermostat, drive belts, and front cam/crank seals at the same time - labor to access these parts is the bulk of the job. Use OEM Aisin or Toyota/Mitsuboshi belt. Verify cam and crank timing marks at TDC #1 before reinstalling covers, and rotate the engine two full revolutions by hand to confirm no valve-to-piston contact before cranking with the starter.

rows.title: Front Lower Control Arm Bushing Failure

Press out the worn bushings and press in OEM-rubber or polyurethane replacements (SuperPro SPF3163K is sized specifically for the 1993-1997 GS300). Reinstall, torque pivot bolts to spec with the suspension loaded at ride height (to avoid pre-loading the new bushings), and perform a four-wheel alignment.

rows.title: Engine ECU/ECM electrolytic capacitor leakage (age-related)

This is fine-pitch SMD work, not a first-time soldering job; many owners send the unit to a specialist recap/rebuild service instead.

rows.title: Power Steering Pressure Hose Leak and Pump Whine from Fluid Loss
rows.howToFix: Inspect the pressure hose, return lines, reservoir, and pump area for wetness, then confirm whether the leak is from the crimped hose section or a fitting. Replace the leaking hose or line assembly, refill with the correct fluid, and bleed the system fully; if the pump has been noisy for long, inspect for internal damage. Cleaning the subframe and alternator area is important because leaked fluid can spread widely.

rows.title: U140E/U151E Automatic Transmission Failure from Burned Planetary Gearset and Delayed Engagement
rows.howToFix: Diagnosis usually starts with checking fluid condition, line pressure behavior, and whether engagement delay or flare shifts are present when warm. In most cases, fluid changes do not cure an already failing unit; the durable fix is a quality rebuild or replacement transmission, often with updated hard parts and careful inspection of the cooler and valve body. Many owners also add an auxiliary transmission cooler after replacement to reduce repeat failures.

rows.title: Rear Main Seal / Engine Oil Leak at Timing Cover and Lower Engine Seals
rows.howToFix: Clean the engine thoroughly and use dye or UV tracing to identify the true source, since valve cover, timing cover, and rear main leaks can be misidentified. Repair involves replacing the failed seal or resealing the timing cover, often while addressing nearby components with overlapping labor. If the leak is minor, some owners monitor oil level until the leak worsens enough to justify the labor.

rows.title: Steering Intermediate Shaft Clunk and Loose Steering Feel Over Bumps
rows.howToFix: Road test over small road imperfections to reproduce the column knock, then isolate the sound from the shaft, rack mounts, and front suspension links. Replacement of the intermediate steering shaft is the usual fix; some vehicles also need inspection of rack bushings and front stabilizer links if multiple noises are present. An alignment is not always required but front-end inspection should accompany the repair.

rows.howToFix: Dealer oil consumption test to document the rate. If excessive, piston ring replacement is the definitive fix under Toyota TSB. Check and clean the PCV valve as a first step. Monitor oil level weekly and keep a log of consumption for warranty claims.

rows.title: AC Evaporator Core Refrigerant Leak
rows.howToFix: Replace the AC evaporator core and receiver/drier. This requires full dashboard removal, which is 8-12 hours of labor. Recharge the system with the correct amount of R-134a refrigerant. Replacing the expansion valve at the same time is recommended while the dash is apart.

rows.title: Water Pump Premature Failure
rows.howToFix: Replace the water pump and thermostat assembly. Use OEM Aisin or Denso parts for reliability. Replace the drive belt and tensioner at the same time. Flush the cooling system with new Toyota Super Long Life Coolant during the repair.

rows.title: 8-Speed Automatic Transmission Shudder
rows.howToFix: Perform a transmission fluid drain-and-fill with Toyota WS ATF, which resolves the shudder in most cases. Severe cases may require a torque converter replacement. Do not flush — only drain and refill. Plan to change the fluid every 30,000-40,000 miles despite the "lifetime" fluid claim.
rows.dispositionReason: At least one replacement is conditional on a stated diagnostic result.

rows.title: 12V Battery Discharge and No-Start from Telematics/DCM Staying Awake
rows.howToFix: Diagnosis should start with a battery state-of-health test and a parasitic draw test after all modules are expected to sleep. Dealers typically check for applicable software updates or service bulletins addressing DCM/module sleep behavior, then recharge or replace the battery if it has been damaged by repeated deep discharge. If draw remains high, isolate the offending circuit and verify telematics, gateway, and body ECU software calibration levels.

rows.title: Brake Pedal Vibration/Grinding and Extended Stopping Feel from ABS Actuator Software Logic
rows.howToFix: Road-test the vehicle on the same surface conditions to reproduce the concern and scan the brake/ABS system for stored codes. Dealers should check for calibration updates to the skid control ECU/ABS software and inspect wheel-speed sensor tone rings, tire size uniformity, and suspension components that could trigger false wheel-slip detection. If no hardware fault is found, software reprogramming is the most common corrective path.

rows.title: Front Camera / Millimeter-Wave Radar Misalignment Causing PCS and Driver-Assist Warnings
rows.howToFix: Inspect the windshield camera area and front radar emblem area for dirt, condensation, damage, or non-OEM replacement parts. Perform a scan for ADAS-related DTCs, then complete static/dynamic calibration of the forward recognition camera and millimeter-wave radar if alignment is out of spec. If warnings persist, dealers may apply software updates or replace a faulty sensor/module after confirming power, ground, and network integrity.

rows.title: Infotainment Screen Freezing, Wireless CarPlay/Android Auto Dropouts, and Rebooting Head Unit
rows.howToFix: First verify the head unit has the latest Lexus Interface software and update the connected phone OS. Delete and re-pair the phone, test both wireless and wired connections, and check for TSBs or dealer software campaigns addressing multimedia instability. If the unit continues freezing or rebooting, dealers may replace the display/audio ECU or related USB hub after documenting the failure.

rows.title: AC Compressor Clutch and Bearing Failure
rows.howToFix: Replace the AC compressor, receiver/drier, and expansion valve. Flush the entire AC system to remove any metal debris from the failed compressor. Recharge with R-134a refrigerant. If debris is found, the condenser should also be replaced to prevent contaminating the new compressor.

rows.title: Dashboard Melting and Sticky Surface
rows.howToFix: Dashboard replacement under Lexus Customer Support Program ZE7. The SC430 is covered under the same program as the ES, IS, and RX. Contact Lexus corporate if the dealer is unresponsive.

rows.title: Timing Belt Service Critical Interval
rows.howToFix: Replace the timing belt, tensioner, idler pulleys, and water pump as a complete kit every 90,000 miles or 9 years, whichever comes first. Age-based replacement is particularly important for SC430s that accumulate low annual mileage, as the belt rubber degrades with age regardless of mileage.

rows.title: A340E Automatic Transmission Wear (Overdrive Slip / Torque-Converter Shudder)
rows.howToFix: Perform a proper fluid and filter service using Toyota Type T-IV ATF as preventive care. If shudder/slip is already present, address the torque converter, valve body, and shift solenoids; a full A340E rebuild (roughly $1,800-$2,500) is the fix for advanced wear.
rows.dispositionReason: The remedy is a service, tool, consumable, or fluid procedure rather than a repair part.

rows.title: Distributor Cap & Rotor Cracking / Ignition Misfire (Non-VVT-i 1992-1997)
rows.howToFix: Replace the distributor cap and rotor (or a good remanufactured distributor if the shaft/bearing is worn); replace the valve cover gasket and spark-plug tube seals if oil is present in the plug wells, and inspect/clean the throttle body. Replace brittle plug wires as preventive maintenance.

rows.title: Front Lower Control Arm Bushing & Ball Joint Wear (Clunk Over Bumps)
rows.howToFix: Replace worn bushings (OEM rubber or polyurethane) to eliminate the clunk; if the integral ball joint is also worn, replace the complete lower control arm assembly (later-gen Supra arms interchange; note JZA70 arms do NOT fit). Do both sides and align afterward.

rows.title: Power Steering Pump Seal Leak Contaminating the Alternator
rows.howToFix: Reseal or replace the power steering pump before fluid reaches the alternator; clean/inspect the alternator, and replace it if already fluid-soaked. Address the pressure control valve if it is the leak source. Doing both the pump and alternator together is common practice when the alternator is contaminated.

rows.title: Power Window Regulator Nylon Carrier Failure
rows.howToFix: Replace the window regulator (OEM or quality aftermarket); replace the dried/worn outer window sweeps to reduce drag. Temporary adhesive/J-B Weld repairs of the carrier are known to fail after only a handful of cycles; durable DIY fixes reinforce the nylon carrier with drilled holes and metal.

rows.title: VVT-i Cam Gear O-Ring / Intake Cam Seal Oil Leak (1998-2000 VVT-i 2JZ-GE)
rows.howToFix: Replace the VVT-i cam gear O-ring (aftermarket Viton/FKM rebuild kit) and/or the front intake camshaft oil seal. Inspect the timing-belt-area seals at the same time and replace the timing belt if due since access overlaps. Use OEM or high-temp Viton seals to prevent recurrence. Dealers typically only sell the complete VVT-i gear (~$350) rather than the O-ring alone.

rows.title: Climate Control LCD Pixel Fade and Dim Backlighting
rows.howToFix: Remove the climate control unit (held in by trim clips and two screws) and either send it to a specialist like Tanin Auto Electronix for LCD/bulb refurbishment, or DIY the repair using a replacement LCD screen and LED bulb kit. The fix typically restores full functionality with a lifetime warranty from reputable rebuilders. Avoid generic 12V replacement bulbs as they produce uneven brightness compared to the rest of the dash.

rows.title: CVT Hesitation and Sluggish Response
rows.howToFix: Update to the latest transmission ECU calibration at the dealer, which improves tip-in response. Use Sport mode for situations requiring quicker response. The UX250h hybrid has better low-speed response than the UX200 due to the electric motor providing instant torque.

rows.title: Infotainment System Lag and Touchpad Frustration
rows.howToFix: Update infotainment software to the latest version. The 2020+ models can have Apple CarPlay/Android Auto added, which dramatically improves the user experience. Use voice commands for navigation and phone functions to avoid the touchpad entirely.
